column1: # The scenario tiers: which native modules and kits answer which question,
# grouped by how long a run takes.  tools/scenario_suite.py reads this file;
# docs/testing.md "Scenario tiers" says how to run a tier against an image set,
# and planning/scenarios-2026-10-04.md is the coverage map it was cut from.
#   TIER  module  tests.MODULE[.Class]  QUESTIONS  why it is in this tier
#   TIER  env     NAME=VALUE            QUESTIONS  what the opt-in turns on
#   TIER  tool    COMMAND               QUESTIONS  a kit hbox_native.sh cannot launch
# QUESTIONS are the coverage map's codes: DUR durability across crash cuts,
# ARU accepted/refused/uncertain distinct, IDEM idempotent resend, BND bounded
# work per step, MEM (F1/F8), LAT (F4), FSYNC (F3), OPEN (F6), PEER, BP, WEB,
# AUTH, CUR consumer cursor, RCON remote consumer, IDN store identity, RDR
# reader conformance, CKPT checkpoint/reclaim, OPS operator/control, INTEROP
# real external software on the other side (INN, stock reader clients).
# A tool COMMAND runs on hbox from a tree of the image's revision ($T) with
# $IMAGES = /tank/fn/images/SHA and $OUT a fresh scratch directory; under
# swarm-build, one at a time, on a quiet box when it measures.
# Only modules that drive an image belong here: a source-reading or -mock
# module answers none of these questions (the coverage map lists them apart).
# peer: "can a stranger's server peer with us safely and usefully" (ember,
# 2026-10-04: the first external collaborator peers with the next redeploy).
# Push and pull both ways, catch-up after a gap, IHAVE/CHECK/TAKETHIS, NEWNEWS
# with wildmats and HDR/XPAT past the cache, a misbehaving peer never pinning
# the owner, peer credentials, and real INN on the other side of the wire.
